reader.requirement: At --std 85, for a relative file in random or dynamic access mode, DELETE removes the record whose relative record number is the current content of the RELATIVE KEY item (any numeric usage), and when no such record exists (number 0, beyond the file, never written, already deleted) the invalid key condition exists: status 23, the INVALID KEY phrase runs, or without one the USE procedure.

edition-consulted.switches: below 2002 the INVALID KEY phrase is required unless a USE applies (§1985:VIII.4.3.3 SR2); compile-time only

reader.edition-search: grep Edition/DialectLevel/DialectBehavior in KeyedIoEmitter.EmitDelete, RelativeConnector.Delete and KeyedStore.Delete: none; the key is set by FileSetRelativeKey from the RELATIVE KEY item at every edition
reader.witnesses-cover: part: g85_f23_03 covers random and dynamic DELETE of an existing record, a deleted one and a never-written one; not key 0, a key beyond the file, a COMP key, the USE path without INVALID KEY, or a key set by READ NEXT

probes.printed: K0 IK 23 / K999 IK 23 / K50 (no INVALID KEY): USE D=23 / K4 00 (PIC 9(3) COMP key) / READ NEXT sets KD=007 then DELETE K7 00 / DEL7AGAIN IK 23; identical at --std 2023
probes.expected: the record named by the key is removed; a missing record is the invalid key condition, 23 (VIII.1.3.4 GRL2.3b1)

citations.check: OK  §1985:VIII.4.3.4 GR3  (4.3.4 General Rules)  the text is in GR3
OK  §1985:VIII.1.3.4  (1.3.4 I-O Status)  the text is in the clause; it lies in GRL2.3b.1

reader.notes: The emitter loads the RELATIVE KEY item into the connector before each random/dynamic DELETE, and the connector answers 23 for slot < 1 or an absent slot before removing anything. The INVALID KEY arm fires on the 2x family only, and without the phrase the USE procedure runs.

refuter.evidence: Probe refute-1985-131/d56.cob (runs/d56-001, --std 85), dynamic access: READ key 2 then READ NEXT reaches record 3 (KD=003), MOVE 5 TO KD, DELETE -> 'DK5 NIK 00'; record 3 still reads 'R3 00 D_03' and record 5 is the invalid key 'R5 IK 23', so the DELETE follows the relative key's current content, not the position the READ NEXT left. Random access with a one-digit PIC 9 key: DELETE key 9 'DR9 NIK 00', then READ key 9 'RR9 IK 23'. Both INVALID KEY and NOT INVALID KEY arms fire as GR8 says. cite.py: OK §1985:VIII.4.3.4 GR3 (the text is in GR3).
